claims.text: The starting material is molten Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Combining controlled cooling rates with ultrasonic treatment can increase amorphous retention in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Combining controlled cooling rates with ultrasonic treatment can increase the thermal stability of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Controlled cooling and ultrasonic treatment refine the alloy's grain structure.
Grain-structure refinement inhibits extensive primary crystallization.
Ultrasonic treatment reduces nucleation sites in the alloy.
Reducing nucleation sites inhibits extensive primary crystallization.
The untreated baseline exhibits extensive primary crystallization during rapid cooling, slower cooling, and subsequent reheating.
Cooling rates from 10^2 to 10^4 K/s are relevant boundaries for the proposed intervention.
A reheating temperature of up to 800 °C is a relevant boundary for testing the proposed behavior.
The intervention is predicted to improve amorphous retention relative to the alloy's reported glass-formation and crystallization behavior.
The intervention is predicted to improve thermal stability relative to the alloy's reported glass-formation and crystallization behavior.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes grain refinement to ultrasound while simultaneously attributing the effect to ultrasonic reduction of nucleation sites. Grain refinement and nucleation-site reduction are not reconciled and imply potentially opposing nucleation behavior.
The proposed intervention is not single: it combines controlled cooling with ultrasonic treatment, so the individual contribution of ultrasound is confounded with the cooling protocol.
